What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Age: 69
Sex: Male
Date of Admission: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient was admitted with severely symptomatic atrial fibrillation (AF) requiring multiple cardioversions. He had a history of an implantable cardiac monitor, left bundle branch block with an ejection fraction of 25%, and a cardiac resynchronization therapy device (CRT-D). The patient underwent uncomplicated pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using radiofrequency (RF) via the SANS FLUORO technique. There were no complications during or after the procedure. The patient was discharged the following day and remained free of AF at his three- and six-month follow-up visits.

HISTORY AND FINDINGS:
The patient had previously undergone successful implantation of the Optimizer™ III device as part of a clinical trial. The preprocedure chest radiograph showed increased scar burden in the left atrium (LA) based on voltage mapping, with ablation lesions showing the left atrial roof and posterior line. Post-PVI, entrance and exit blocks were demonstrated. The postprocedure CRT-D check revealed no change in lead sensing, threshold, or impedance values.
DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
PROCEDURE/TREATMENT:
Uncomplicated pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using radiofrequency (RF) via the SANS FLUORO technique.

FOLLOW-UP:
The patient remained free of AF at his three- and six-month follow-up visits.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
The patient is instructed to follow up with their healthcare provider as recommended.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
N/A

DISCHARGE CONDITION:
The patient was discharged in stable condition.

text:
The principal diagnosis is **atrial fibrillation**, but the summary doesn't specify the type, so the most accurate code from the available documentation is **I48.9 (Atrial fibrillation, unspecified)**.

The admission was for severely symptomatic AF requiring multiple cardioversions, and the PVI ablation treated that condition. The type of AF determines the code, and the record doesn't state it:

- **Paroxysmal AF:** I48.0
- **Persistent AF:** I48.1 (ICD-10-AM 11th edition subdivides this into I48.11 longstanding persistent and I48.19 other persistent)
- **Chronic/permanent AF:** I48.2 (I48.21 permanent)

Repeated cardioversions suggest persistent AF, but coders shouldn't infer the type from procedures. A clinical documentation query to the treating cardiologist would be needed to assign a more specific code. The withheld diagnosis section also means I48.9 should be verified against the full record.
